message.content:
**Logistic regression** is a statistical method used to model the relationship between one or more predictor variables and a binary (two‑class) outcome. Instead of predicting a continuous value, it predicts the probability that the outcome belongs to a particular class. ### Key points | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Outcome** | Binary (e.g., 0/1, yes/no, success/failure). | | **Model form** | Uses the logistic (sigmoid) function to map a linear combination of predictors to a probability between 0 and 1:
\(\displaystyle P(Y=1|X)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-(\beta_0+\beta_1X_1+\dots+\beta_pX_p)}}\) | | **Link function** | Logit link: \(\text{logit}(P)=\ln\!\big(\frac{P}{1-P}\big)=\beta_0+\beta_1X_1+\dots+\beta_pX_p\). | | **Estimation** | Parameters \(\beta\) are estimated by maximum likelihood (MLE). | | **Interpretation** | Coefficients represent the change in the log‑odds of the outcome per unit change in the predictor. Exponentiating gives odds ratios. | | **Extensions** | • **Multinomial logistic regression** for more than two unordered categories.
• **Ordinal logistic regression** for ordered categories.
• **Regularized logistic regression** (L1/L2 penalties) for high‑dimensional data. | ### Example Suppose you want to predict whether a patient has a disease (1) or not (0) based on age and blood pressure: \[ \text{logit}(P)=\beta_0 + \beta_1(\text{age}) + \beta_2(\text{BP}) \] After fitting the model, you might find: - \(\beta_1 = 0.05\) → each additional year of age increases the odds of disease by \(e^{0.05}\approx 1.05\) (5% higher odds). - \(\beta_2 = 0.02\) → each additional mmHg of blood pressure increases the odds by \(e^{0.02}\approx 1.02\) (2% higher odds). ### When to use logistic regression - Predicting a binary outcome (e.g., spam vs. not spam, disease vs. healthy). - When you have a mix of continuous and categorical predictors. - When you need interpretable coefficients (odds ratios). Logistic regression is a foundational tool in statistics, machine learning, epidemiology, social sciences, and many other fields.
